subject: RFI: GPU tiering, SLA tradeoffs, and fallback policy for LLM inference

Subject: RFI: GPU tiering & fallback policy for LLM inference

Jonas —

Thanks for taking this RFI. Attached is DataCorp's short questionnaire focused on how vendors tier GPU capacity for different model families, your policy for graceful degradation/fallback (e.g., CPU or smaller quantized variants), and how throughput SLOs change by tier. We're particularly interested in: 1) recommended GPU types for stable conversational throughput at 2k tokens/session, 2) the tradeoffs between reserved capacity and burst lanes, and 3) response behavior when reserved capacity is exhausted.

We're running this with our platform team and procurement in parallel. Can you confirm you can return the filled questionnaire and a short capacity scenario matrix by EOD Wednesday (2026-11-18)? We'll use that to shortlist vendors for an on-site POC.

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifying points that will drive our prioritization:

- For quantized variants (e.g., int8/4), can you share typical throughput improvement and cost delta relative to FP16 for large decoder models?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@datacorp.com>, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-17T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFI: GPU tiering & fallback policy for LLM inference

Alice —

Thanks for the questions. Below is a condensed technical response; we've also populated the spreadsheet with three concrete scenarios and attached a CSV export. High level first, then the scenario bullets.

High-level answers: 
- Automatic fallback: Redwood supports configurable fallback policies. By default we attempt soft-fallbacks within the same GPU tier (model variant / lower-max-seq) and then, if configured, fallback to a quantized CPU path or smaller quantized model (int8 / int4) hosted on cheaper instances. Fallbacks are policy-driven (customer-configurable) — we do not silently send inference to CPU unless explicitly allowed.
- Quantization delta: For large decoder-only models (7B-70B), int8 typically yields ~1.6–2x throughput vs FP16 with minimal quality drift; int4 can yield ~2.5–3x throughput but with higher quality risk depending on prompt distribution. These are workload-dependent. We include profiles in the workbook.
- 99th percentile latency: We include empirical 95/99 p95/p99 for each scenario assuming the KV cache hit rates in the workbook. Note p99 widens significantly in spiky workloads if burst capacity is shared across many tenants; we call this out and recommend reserved lanes for latency-sensitive routes.

Scenario matrix (summary):
1) Steady-conversational (default): target 2k tokens/session, 250 concurrent sessions sustained
   - Recommended: mix of H100 (reserved) + A100s for overflow; if cost constrained, L4 for small-context sessions.
   - Expected throughput: H100: ~750 tokens/sec per GPU (decoder heavy, batch-aware), A100-80GB: ~620 t/s; L4: ~220 t/s.
   - Sizing (250 concurrent, 2k tokens/session, 1.6 sec median turn): reserve 6 H100s (with autoscale buffer +1) to meet p95 < 180 ms; p99 ~420 ms.
2) Spiky-burst (PEAK): short bursts up to 3x baseline for 10–15 minutes
   - Strategy: reserved baseline (A100) + burst pool (preemptible H100 or lower-cost instances) + automatic overload policy to degrade to int8 variant or lower max-seq.
   - Expected p99 in overflow without reserved lanes: can hit 1.2–2.5s depending on burst concurrency.
3) High-concurrency inference (batch ranking / heavy token throughput): prefer dense A100/H100 pools with session multiplexing; recommend explicit reservation of 70–80% of expected baseline.

Fallback policy examples (customer-configurable):
- Conservative: never fallback to CPU; queue requests and return 503 when queue limit reached.
- Balanced: degrade to int8 quantized variant on overflow, then queue.
- Aggressive-cost: route to CPU-backed int8 when tail latency allowed up to 2s.

Attachments: scenario_matrix.csv (CSV export of the sizing workbook)

We'll add explicit cost-per-token estimates into the workbook for each scenario (we left placeholders in v0.1) and include p99 columns. I've flagged a follow-up note for Neha to compute detailed cost estimates by GPU mix.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Infra Product Lead, Redwood Inference
